## 1. Overview

The EA Product Engagement Model establishes a direct partnership between the EA Practice Office and product organizations, ensuring all product-related work—from sales opportunities through new development, feature enhancements, and maintenance & operations—flows through a single architectural interface for consistency, quality, and enterprise alignment.
page_texts.5:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#21-single-architectural-interface]

### 2.1 Single Architectural Interface

- **Product Solution Architect (PSA)** is the sole EA interface for all product-related work
- Direct partnership with Product General Manager and Product Engineering Executive
- Eliminates confusion about when and how to engage EA resources
page_texts.6:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#22-governance-driven-workflow]

### 2.2 Governance-Driven Workflow

Product initiatives enter through three governance entry points:

- **Opportunity Gate** → Product-Specific Sales Efforts
- **Solutioning Gate** → New Product Development & Product Feature Development
- **Delivery & Operations Gate** → Maintenance & Operations (M&O)
page_texts.7:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#23-comprehensive-coverage]

### 2.3 Comprehensive Coverage

ALL product initiatives flow through the assigned Product Solution Architect:

- Product feature development (enhancements and iterations)
- New product development (greenfield and major releases)
- Maintenance & Operations (M&O) activities
- Product-specific sales efforts and proposals
page_texts.8:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#24-direct-partnership-model]

### 2.4 Direct Partnership Model

Three-way collaboration: **Product GM ↔ Product Engineering Executive ↔ EA Product Solution Architect**

- Review, prioritize, and implement initiatives together
- Engineering collaboration between PEE and PSA
- Strategic direction from EA Domain Leads and Senior Leadership
page_texts.9:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#3-ea-product-relationship-model]

## 3. EA-Product Relationship Model

Each product engagement follows a standardized model that defines:

- **Team Structure**: Product leadership, engineering, and EA practice teams
- **Engagement Interaction**: Visual diagram showing how teams collaborate through governance entry points
- **RACI Matrix**: Clear accountability for key activities across product lifecycle
- **Application Portfolio**: Technology assets and platforms

See the [Product Engagement TEMPLATE](TEMPLATE.md) for the detailed engagement model structure. Each product-specific engagement document uses this template to define their unique team composition and collaboration patterns.
page_texts.10:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#4-product-engagement-documentation]

## 4. Product Engagement Documentation

Each product has dedicated engagement documentation detailing:

- Assigned EA Product Solution Architect(s)
- Product-specific architectural considerations
- Technology stack and patterns
- Integration points and dependencies
- Ongoing initiatives and roadmap alignment
- Architectural health metrics

page_texts.13:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#51-for-product-general-managers]

### 5.1 For Product General Managers

1. **Know Your Product Solution Architect**: Each product has an assigned EA PSA
2. **Engage Early**: Involve your PSA at initiative inception (Opportunity, Solutioning, or Delivery gates)
3. **Collaborate Continuously**: Establish recurring touchpoints (weekly/bi-weekly)
4. **Leverage Partnership**: Use PSA for architectural guidance, standards compliance, and governance navigation
page_texts.14:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#52-for-product-engineering-executives]

### 5.2 For Product Engineering Executives

1. **Engineering Collaboration**: Work directly with Product SA on technical implementation
2. **Organizational Relationships**: Maintain connections with Sales Organization and DDI Accounts for broader context
3. **Resource Coordination**: Partner with PSA to identify cross-product dependencies and shared resources
page_texts.15:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#53-for-ea-product-solution-architects]

### 5.3 For EA Product Solution Architects

1. **Domain Expertise**: Build deep understanding of product architecture, roadmap, and business context
2. **Governance Facilitation**: Guide product initiatives through appropriate governance gates (CRB, DRB, ARB, ORT, TOPS, PPR)
3. **Enterprise Rollup**: Aggregate and report product architecture health to EA Practice for portfolio visibility
4. **Standards Advocacy**: Ensure product solutions adhere to enterprise architecture standards and patterns

page_texts.18:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#71-partnership-health-indicators]

### 7.1 Partnership Health Indicators

- Regular PGM-PSA touchpoint attendance (weekly/bi-weekly)
- Initiative alignment with governance entry points (90%+ mapped correctly)
- Architectural review completion within SLA (95%+ on-time)
page_texts.19:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#72-architectural-quality-metrics]

### 7.2 Architectural Quality Metrics

- Standards compliance rate across product initiatives
- Architectural debt trends (reducing over time)
- Technical risk identification and mitigation effectiveness
page_texts.20:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#73-portfolio-visibility]

### 7.3 Portfolio Visibility

- Product architecture health rollup to Enterprise Portfolio View
- Cross-product dependency identification and management
- Resource allocation optimization across products
page_texts.22:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#81-new-product-general-managers]

### 8.1 New Product General Managers

1. Review the [EA-Product Relationship Model](../../organizational-structure.md#ea-product-relationship-model)
2. Connect with your assigned EA Product Solution Architect (see product-specific page)
3. Schedule introductory 1:1 meeting to understand engagement model
4. Map existing initiatives to appropriate governance entry points
page_texts.23:
[foundation/engagements/product/README.md#82-new-ea-product-solution-architects]

### 8.2 New EA Product Solution Architects

1. Meet with Product GM and Product Engineering Executive
2. Review product roadmap and strategic priorities
3. Assess current architectural landscape and identify gaps
4. Establish recurring collaboration cadence
5. Document product-specific engagement considerations
